From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 19, 2026 at 10:12 AM PST
Subject: Perf-canary in Console: internal surfacing v1 + path to customer-facing regression views

Marissa,

We’re aligning the perf regression canary rollout (phase 1 us-east) and I want to make sure we don’t end up with “Grafana-only tribal knowledge”.

Can you propose what the Console should show internally in v1 (for oncall + runtime), and what we’d need to keep the door open for a customer-facing regression view later?

Constraints from SRE/Telemetry:
- keep it low-cardinality; avoid per-prompt or per-request IDs
- must include enough context to attribute to runtime build / scheduler mode / GPU SKU
- suppress false positives around deploy windows and warmups

If you can outline:
1) internal UX: where it lives, what’s on the page, and what links out
2) data/API requirements (even if it’s “we just deep-link to Grafana now”)

…that’ll help me close the loop with leadership.

Mateo

—
Mateo Alvarez
Exec Sponsor, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 19, 2026 at 1:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary in Console: internal surfacing v1 + path to customer-facing regression views

Yep. Proposal for v1 (internal-only):

Console location:
- Console → Operations → “Performance Canary” (internal feature flag)
- This is not meant to replace Grafana; it’s a curated entry point with the right defaults + links.

What it shows (v1):
A) “Active regressions” table (last 24h)
- Columns: Model, Region, Slice (GPU SKU + scheduler_mode), Metric (p95 latency / tokens_sec), Regression %, Baseline (rolling 7d median vs pinned known-good), First seen, Last deploy annotation (runtime_version + git_sha), Status (New / Acknowledged / Suppressed)
- Clicking a row opens a detail drawer.

B) Detail drawer for one regression
- Sparkline: last 6h + last 7d context
- Baseline definition text (so oncall doesn’t have to guess)
- “Context” block (must be in payload / labels): runtime_build, runtime_version, git_sha, gpu_sku, scheduler_mode, selected_kernel_id (if gated), batch stats summary (prefill/decode counts, max_seq_len)
- Buttons:
  1) Open Grafana (pre-filtered)
  2) Open Runbook
  3) Open last runtime deploy diff (if we have it)

C) “Coverage” section
- Models x regions matrix (simple checkmarks + last successful sample timestamp)
- Any slices currently excluded due to cardinality budget.

What we need now to keep customer-facing path open:
- stable naming/semantics for the regression object (metric, slice, baseline, threshold, suppression) so we can expose later without redoing everything
- a concept of “slice” in the UI that can be translated (for customers we may hide scheduler_mode/kernel_id but keep region + model + deployment)

I’ll attach a rough mock (table + drawer). Happy to walk it in 15m.

Attachment: Perf Canary - Console surfacing v1 (mock) v3.png

Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 19, 2026 at 3:10 PM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary in Console: internal surfacing v1 + path to customer-facing regression views

+1 on the curated entry point.

Telemetry constraints / suggestions so we don’t paint ourselves into a corner:

1) “Active regressions” source of truth
- The detector can emit a single event/metric with a compact label set (model, region, gpu_sku, scheduler_mode, metric_name, severity)
- Console can read from that (or from an incident-bot webhook store) rather than trying to compute baselines in Console.

2) Cardinality
- Please don’t rely on selected_kernel_id being present everywhere. We can gate it behind source=perf-canary and sample it, but it’s too expensive as a top-level label.
- Better: include kernel_id in the alert payload (log/trace attachment) and keep the metric labels minimal.

3) Baseline semantics
- Important to represent baseline type in the UI: rolling_median_7d vs pinned_build (known-good). If the baseline is rolling, make it explicit that we can “learn” regressions (it’s a feature, but people find it confusing).

4) Suppression / deploy windows
- Detector should mark “suppressed=true” or “suppressed_reason=deploy_window” so Console can show “we saw it but did not page”.

If you want, I can help define the “regression object” fields in a way that works for future externalization.

Logan

—
Logan Wright
Telemetry Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary in Console: internal surfacing v1 + path to customer-facing regression views

This looks good, with one strong request from SRE:

- The internal Console page must clearly distinguish:
  (a) “regression detected”
  (b) “regression paged”
  (c) “regression suppressed”

Otherwise we’ll get pinged by folks seeing a regression in a dashboard and assuming oncall ignored it.

Also, for future customer-facing:
- we probably cannot expose anything that implies multi-tenant fleet internals (GPU SKU / scheduler_mode) unless it’s Dedicated/Private where it’s clearly “your fleet”.
- The translation layer you mentioned (“slice” → customer-safe slice) is key. I’d recommend we adopt internal field names now but explicitly mark which are safe to show externally.

One more UX point:
- If we link to Grafana, include a “copy link for incident” button (pre-fills timeframe + filters). This reduces thrash in incident channels.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 20, 2026 at 2:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Perf-canary in Console: internal surfacing v1 + path to customer-facing regression views

Agree on the “detected vs paged vs suppressed” distinction — I’ll bake that into the table as separate badges and make “paged” derive from an alert fire marker (not just threshold breach).

On customer-facing: makes sense to treat “slice” as an internal technical dimension set, and define an external projection. I’ll add a section to the spec:

Internal fields (not necessarily external-safe):
- gpu_sku
- scheduler_mode
- kernel_id / fallback_reason
- batch stats (esp. queue lengths)

External-safe candidates (depending on product tier):
- model
- region
- deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)
- metric (p95 latency / tokens/sec)
- baseline type + regression magnitude
- time window

Implementation option for v1 (to keep scope sane):
- Console page reads a small “regression feed” produced by perf-canary service (or incident-bot) and only deep-links to Grafana for graphs.
- Later: if we decide to show full charts in Console, we can pull from the metrics API using the same regression object keys.

Attaching the notes doc with field suggestions + copy link UX.

Attachment: perf-canary-console-surface-v1-notes.txt

Marissa

This is exactly what I needed.

Next steps:
- Marissa: please post the spec draft in Confluence + link it in ENG-2847 as “Console entry point for perf-canary (internal)”.
- Logan: can you sanity-check the proposed regression object fields against the metric spec + cardinality budget? (esp. how we represent suppression + baseline type)
- Sean: once we have a first pass, let’s ensure the page wording aligns with the paging policy (so it doesn’t imply “SRE missed an alert”).

If we can get the internal page (even minimal table + links) ready by the us-east phase 1 start, that will materially reduce time-to-triage.

Mateo
